description: PPMtools is a Python package developed in the US Environmental Protection Agency repository for modelling premise plumbing systems. It represents houses, people and fixtures in an agent-based model and includes Monte Carlo functions for generating household water-use patterns. Users configure the building and its occupants; the resulting patterns can support simulation of water movement within a plumbing network. Its spatial coverage is an individual building, with no fixed geographic or observation period. The README identifies dependencies on WNTR and EPANET version 2.2 or newer. Source code is publicly accessible under the MIT licence at no charge. The repository explicitly labels the code as draft and says it has not been reviewed or cleared by EPA. It also describes a water-age example as forthcoming, so that example is not treated as completed validation. Related records are EPANET and WNTR. Only the repository documentation was inspected; the code and included network files were not downloaded or run.
